summary: In-schema CoT: name 7 unknowns, then question each
hypothesis: Forcing the model to explicitly name the 7 most decision-critical unknowns before phrasing questions would stop it defaulting to generic catch-alls, because committing to the unknowns first should condition and sharpen the questions that follow — all in a single call, avoiding the compounding weak-judgment of multi-call think-first pipelines.
technique: A single on-device FM call using a guided output schema that forces the model to first fill a `criticalUnknowns: [String].count(7)` field (naming the 7 highest-leverage unknowns) before writing one question per unknown in order — in-schema CoT via field-ordering — anchored by a worked reasoning demo plus exp011's contrastive RAG few-shot exemplars.
result: Scored 0.247 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), the worst of the RAG-derived family and a sharp regression of −0.073 below the exp003/exp011 plateau (~0.32) and −0.060 below the 0.307 baseline; rubric atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=3, nonRed=3. The hypothesis was falsified: the 3B model fills the reasoning slot with the same generic/confused content it would emit anyway, hard-wiring wrong coverage into the questions, and the added abstraction actively introduced catastrophic perspective errors (e.g. asking "how much experience do you have as a therapist?" to the user). Discarded.
